record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Computation as Questions about Two-Way Deterministic Pushdown Automaton Languages
record.original_question: Is the class P-TIME of polynomial-time decidable languages equal to the class P-SPACE of languages decidable by deterministic Turing machines using polynomial space?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let P denote the class of all languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine $M$ and a polynomial $p$ such that $M$ decides membership in $L$ and, on every input $x$, halts within $p(|x|)$ steps. Let PSPACE denote the class of all languages $L \subseteq \{0,1\}^*$ for which there exists a deterministic Turing machine $M$ and a polynomial $q$ such that $M$ decides membership in $L$ and, on every input $x$, uses at most $q(|x|)$ tape cells of work space.

Determine whether P = PSPACE.
artifact.status_search_result: The question of whether P equals PSPACE is a long-standing major open problem in computational complexity theory. It is widely believed that P ≠ PSPACE, but no proof of separation (or equality) is known.

status_evidence.title: P versus PSPACE - Complexity Zoo / Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: It is known that P ⊆ PSPACE, but whether the inclusion is strict is a major open problem.
